title: Move each PIM Manager app and job to its own identity
purpose: Moves each PIM Manager app and job of one install from its current identity (system-assigned, or a shared user-assigned identity) to its own user-assigned identity id-pim-<role>, with the same rights, proven, and only then removes the old identity's copied rights.
whenToRun: Once per install for the identity naming standard (one user-assigned identity per role, named id-pim-<role>). First without -Apply (the plan, read-only), then -Apply -Role <role> one role at a time. A role whose proof is still pending (a job that has not run since the switch) is finished by running the same command again after that run.

runAs.name: The Invardia Support app's session in this window (PIM's REST context) with AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All, RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory and GroupMember.ReadWrite.All
runAs.why: Reads the old identity's application permission grants, PIM group memberships and directory role assignments, and gives the same to the new identity; removes them from the old one after the proof.

runAs.name: Contributor + User Access Administrator
runAs.why: Creates the user-assigned identity, attaches it to the container apps and jobs, writes Azure role assignments (Key Vault, AcrPull, the resource group) and Key Vault access policies, starts the database job and the proof run.

runAs.name: User Access Administrator (only with -SupportHasRootAccess)
runAs.why: Copies a right the old identity holds at the tenant root (the engine's Reader). Without it that right is a customer step with the exact command.

changes.object: the user-assigned managed identity id-pim-<role>, tagged pim-component=<role>
changes.why: One identity per role, named by the standard.
changes.undo: Invoke-PimArm -Method DELETE on the identity (the command is in the run record).

changes.object: every application permission (appRoleAssignments) the old identity holds, given to id-pim-<role>
changes.permission: the same application permissions as the old identity (application permission)
changes.why: The same rights on the new identity before anything switches.
changes.undo: DELETE the assignment on the new identity (the command is in the run record).

changes.object: membership of PIM's own groups (grp-pim-*, members/$ref) the old identity is in
changes.permission: member of the same PIM groups
changes.why: The SQL admin group and the other PIM groups the role needs.
changes.undo: Remove the member (the command is in the run record).

changes.object: the directory role assignments of the old identity, given to the new one (for example Fabric Administrator for the engine's Power BI reads)
changes.undo: DELETE the directory role assignment (the command is in the run record).

changes.object: owner of PIM's own product app registrations (owners/$ref) -- the UPDATER role only, the identity that owns them
changes.permission: owner of the same PIM registrations
changes.why: The updater proves and keeps its app-registration ownership as its new identity.
changes.undo: Remove the owner (the command is in the run record).

changes.object: the sign-in front's federated credential (federatedIdentityCredentials) on the PIM Manager registration, for the new web identity -- the WEB role only
changes.permission: a federated credential trusting the new identity
changes.why: The sign-in front signs in as the web identity, with no secret.
changes.undo: DELETE the credential (the command is in the run record).

changes.object: every Azure role assignment held directly by the old identity (Key Vault RBAC, AcrPull, Storage Blob Data Contributor for the as-built report, the resource group, the tenant root with -SupportHasRootAccess)
changes.why: The same rights on the new identity before anything switches.
changes.undo: DELETE the role assignment (the command is in the run record).

changes.object: the old identity's access policy permissions, given to the new identity
changes.permission: the same key / secret / certificate permissions
changes.scope: the vaults of the PIM resource group
changes.undo: accessPolicies/remove for the new identity (the command is in the run record).

changes.object: the contained database user id-pim-<role>, made by one run of the in-network database job (ca-pim-dbinit)
changes.permission: the role's database roles from the access catalog (for example pim_engine; the updater also db_ddladmin)
changes.why: The new identity signs in to the database with its own user.
changes.undo: The user stays harmless until the switch; remove it with the database job if wanted.

changes.object: each app / job of the role: the new identity attached, the registry pull identity, Key Vault secret references and PIM_ManagedIdentityClientId (and every setting equal to the old client id) switched to it
changes.scope: the PIM apps and jobs of the role
changes.why: The app / job signs in as its own identity.
changes.undo: Set-PimIdentityMoveSwitch with the old identity (the command is in the run record).

changes.object: one run of the engine job (and of each job in -StartJobRoles) for the proof
changes.why: Proves the role works as the new identity before any old right is removed.
changes.undo: Nothing to undo: a normal run.

changes.object: ONLY after the proof: the old identity's copied rights (application permissions, PIM group memberships, directory roles, Azure role assignments, access policies); a shared user-assigned identity is detached from the app and keeps its rights while anything else uses it; a system-assigned identity stays enabled
changes.why: One identity per role; no right left on the identity that no longer runs the role.
changes.undo: Each removal has its exact re-grant command in the run record.

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: The subscription of the PIM install.

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: The resource group of the PIM install.

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: The tenant id (names the tenant root management group).

parameters.name: Apply
parameters.help: Move the roles in -Role. Without it the script only plans.

parameters.name: Role
parameters.help: The roles to move with -Apply: web, engine, updater, downlink, publish, requests, mcp, dbinit, asbuilt.

parameters.name: SupportHasRootAccess
parameters.help: The Support app holds User Access Administrator at the tenant root of this install. Without it every root right is a customer step.

parameters.name: ExtraScopes
parameters.help: More scopes to read the old identity's Azure roles at (for example a registry outside the subscription).

parameters.name: PimGroupNames
parameters.help: More PIM group names whose membership moves (grp-pim-* always does).

parameters.name: StartJobRoles
parameters.help: The roles whose job is started once for the proof.

parameters.name: NoCleanup
parameters.help: Stop after the proof; the old rights stay.

parameters.name: NeedOnly
parameters.help: From a SHARED identity copy only the rights the role needs (the product's rights map per role); every right left behind is listed as not copied. The SQL admin group goes only to the database job. A shared identity nothing uses any more loses all its rights at its last clean-up.

parameters.name: LogDir
parameters.help: Where the plan and the per-role records are written as JSON.

readsOnly: the container apps, jobs, user-assigned identities, key vaults, SQL servers and storage accounts of the resource group
the Azure role assignments of the old and the new identity (at the subscription and every scope above and below it)
the application permission grants, PIM group memberships and directory role assignments of the old and the new identity
the new revision / the job runs after the switch (the proof)
whatIf: Without -Apply the script is read-only either way. With -Apply -WhatIf it reads everything, prints the plan and, per role, one line for each step it would take (create, grant, switch, prove, remove) -- nothing is written.
undo: Every run writes a record to -LogDir with each change in order and its exact undo command; a failed run prints them newest first. Nothing old is removed before the proof.
